newsitem.title: JAMAICA: 'I have lost a friend,' Castro says of Manley.
newsitem.headline: 'I have lost a friend,' Castro says of Manley.

text.p: Cuban President Fidel Castro said on Tuesday he had lost a friend with the death of former Jamaican Prime Minister Michael Manley.

In a statement issued through the Cuban Embassy in Kingston, Castro described the former Jamaican premier, with whom he had especially close ties in the 1970s, as a "lucid thinker, energetic and charming speaker, trade union and political leader (and) vibrant social organiser."
He said: "I have lost a friend with whom I had the privilege to share moments of fruitful exchange and nice company."
Manley maintained close ties with Castro after he left office in 1992 and brokered an unsuccessful bid by British firm Cable & Wireless to acquire the Cuban state-owned telephone company.
Manley, prime minister of Jamaica from 1972 until 1980 and again from 1989 to 1992, died on Thursday night at the age of 72 after a long battle with prostate cancer.
Jamaica has declared three days of official mourning starting on Friday, when Manley's body will lie in state at the national arena in Kingston. He will be given a state funeral on Sunday.
